articles.title: No cluster kitchens for midday meals in Karnataka, says Education Minister Madhu Bangarappa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Minister says that midday meal workers need not worry about their jobs

Minister for School Education and Literacy Madhu Bangarappa has assured that cluster kitchens (centralised cooking facilities) will not be established under the scheme providing midday meals to schoolchildren (Classes I to X) in the State. He said that midday meal workers need not worry about their jobs.

On Monday, S. Balan, honorary president of Akshara Dasoha (Midday Meal Workers’ Union), met the Minister at his residence and submitted a list of demands, including not entertaining the idea of cluster kitchens.

The delegation also sought a hike in monthly remuneration, citing the example of Keralam, where workers are paid ₹12,000, compared with ₹4,600 to ₹4,700 in Karnataka. Mr. Bangarappa said he would discuss the demand with the Chief Minister. “It is to our government’s credit that we previously raised the retirement corpus for midday meal workers to ₹40,000,” he said.
He advised the union to meet Union government officials, noting that the midday meal scheme is not solely funded by the State government and involves participation from the Centre as well.

Mr. Balan also raised concerns over substandard grains and rice being supplied to government schools to cook midday meals for children. The Minister sought precise details on where such incidents were occurring, promising strict action.

The delegation submitted a memorandum to the Minister outlining various demands, including the establishment of joint bank accounts for school headmasters and head cooks, a retirement corpus of at least ₹1 lakh, and a monthly pension of ₹5,000.

articles.title: Voters’ personal data submitted though Form 6 was exposed on ECI citizen service portal, claims report
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: While records going back to 2023 were verified for the report, there was nothing to suggest earlier records were protected, so the exposure may be longer

For at least three years, the personal data that voters submitted to the Election Commission of India through Form 6, the application for registration as an elector, was exposed on its Citizen Service Portal (https://voters.eci.gov.in/ ) to anyone with a login, claims a report by ‘Charchagram’, a civic-tech initiative for building tools for enhancing transparency and accountability in public systems of India.
It said that while records going back to 2023 were verified for this report, there was nothing to suggest earlier records were protected, so the exposure may be longer.
According to the report, using ECI published data, it estimates that at least seven crore Form 6 enrolments took place in this period.

Each Form 6 application holds a citizen’s name, their relative’s name, gender, phone number, email, home address, photograph, Aadhaar details, age-proof documents, and address-proof documents, among other details.

“We audited the front-end code available in public. And while auditing, [we] found that there is URL through which anyone can access Form 6 data of other voters,” said Saurav Rajput, a data scientist at Charchagram.
Opening “voters.eci.gov.in/form6?refId= ” returned a web-page showing all the applicants’ details to any logged-in user, regardless of who the applicant was.

“The reference IDs follow a predictable state, constituency, type and date/sequence pattern. The server did not check that the application belonged to the person asking. The predictability of the reference ID amplifies this security issue, since any user can scrape the data one by one in large volumes,” according to the report.
Following the revelation, Charchagram says it reported the matter privately to the ECI and to CERT-In.
CERT-In is the national nodal agency for responding to computer security incidents as and when they occur.
“We asked for a fix within seven days and for written acknowledgement and confirmation when it was done,” Mr. Rajput said.

articles.title: A.P. CM calls for wider use of AI in healthcare, agriculture to improve public services
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chandrababu Naidu directs senior officials to take up capacity-building programmes to enhance the technological capabilities and professional skills of government employees

Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has called for the wider application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) across various sectors, including healthcare and agriculture, to improve service delivery, administrative efficiency and government revenue.

Reviewing the functioning of the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) with senior officials of various departments on Sunday, Mr. Naidu stressed the need to leverage modern technology and the AI stack to simplify government services and improve the performance of departments.

He directed officials to take measures to ensure that public services were delivered more efficiently and promptly. He also called for capacity-building programmes to enhance the technological capabilities and professional skills of government employees.

Stressing that delays in addressing public grievances should be avoided, the Chief Minister has directed officials to expedite the resolution of complaints received through the Public Grievance Redressal System. A positive public perception of government services was essential for improving governance and called upon departments to regularly review their performance and address shortcomings in monitoring mechanisms, he said.

Mr. Naidu said the government was using Revenue and Legal AI stacks to analyse various issues and identify ways to improve departmental performance. Data-driven decision-making would become increasingly important in governance in the coming years, he observed.

Referring to the recent local body elections, he said the results could serve as one of the indicators of the government’s performance. He asked senior departmental officials to strengthen monitoring mechanisms and ensure better delivery of services to the public.
Senior officials from the Social Welfare, BC Welfare, Minority Welfare, Finance, Municipal Administration and Energy departments, besides RTGS officials, participated in the review meeting.

articles.title: Government will explore all possible ways to avoid electricity restriction in Keralam, says Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Sunny Joseph announces that the Idukki and Cheruthoni dams will be opened to tourists starting December 1

The government will explore all possible ways to avoid power restrictions in the State, Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph has said. Addressing a Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) review meeting at Thodupuzha in Idukki on Monday, Joseph said that due to the El Niño effect, rainfall has been largely reduced in the State, affecting the storage levels of hydroelectric dams. “Compared to the previous year, the water level in Idukki, including major hydel dams, is more than 20% below storage this year. Presently, there is only 60% storage in the hydel dams in the State,” the Minister said.

Mr. Joseph further noted that the government will t launch initiatives to arrange power from other sources. According to KSEB data, the water level in the Idukki dam on Monday was 2,368.9 feet (63%), compared with 2,384.98 feet (79%) on the same day last year.

During the meeting, the Minister announced that the Idukki and Cheruthoni dams will be opened to tourists starting December 1. He said the decision was taken based on repeated demands from various quarters. The Minister also directed officials to take steps to resume the boating facility at the Anayirankal dam reservoir.

Based on the recommendation of a panel appointed by the High Court to address human-animal conflicts in Chinnakkanal, the boating facility in Anayirankal was suspended following the court’s direction on July 14, 2023. articles.title: Shivamogga airport included in UDAN 6.0 tender process, says MP
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: B.Y. Raghavendra, Shivamogga MP, said that the Union government has decided to include Shivamogga airport in the revised UDAN 6.0 tender process. He expressed hope that the airport would become active again, with several flights operating from there.

Speaking to presspersons in Shivamogga on Monday, Mr. Raghavendra said uncertainty over the airport’s inclusion had persisted for the past 15 to 20 days, and that it now appeared to be clearing. The last date for bids is December 31.

He said that under the earlier version of the scheme, an airport would have a one-year commercial break after three years of Viability Gap Funding (VGF) support for flight operations. This time, following requests from people’s representatives, including himself, the Centre has included the airport in the next tender without any such break. He said this would allow Shivamogga to grow commercially under UDAN over the next five years, and that flight services would follow naturally.

Unlike earlier tenders, the current one does not name specific routes. Airlines have the freedom to choose which routes to operate from Shivamogga, and bidders would be eligible for UDAN subsidy. Mr. Raghavendra said efforts were under way to hold talks with three airlines about their participation in the tender. He thanked the Prime Minister, former Chief Minister B.S. Yediyurappa and Union Minister Pralhad Joshi for their support.

Mr. Raghavendra said the tender process could take until February or March 2027 to be finalised and for operations to begin, which could leave a gap of three to four months. He urged the State government to provide temporary VGF support for two to three months in the interim, at least for the Shivamogga–Bengaluru and Shivamogga–Hyderabad routes, or one of them. If an airline chose these routes under the tender, he said, the State could withdraw its support.
Regarding cargo services and night landing, he said decisions would be taken after a survey based on local demand, crops and export opportunities was conducted.

Flight operations under UDAN from Shivamogga airport ended last week. As a result, the airport built at Sogane, near Shivamogga, has gone silent. It was inaugurated in February 2023 and has been operating since August 2023.

articles.title: 3-member panel meet of KRMB ends without taking any decision on water use
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Telangana strongly opposed to AP’s demand for release of Nagarjunsagar water for use in Krishna Delta System

The three-member committee of the Krishna River Management Board (KRMB) which met here on Monday to discuss the drinking water needs of the two member States — Andhra Pradesh and Telangana — for the next three months ended without taking any decision as Telangana strongly opposed A.P.’s indent of 19 tmc ft water, including 10 tmc ft for Krishna Delta System from Nagarjunasagar dam.

The meeting chaired by Member-Secretary of the river board Satish Kumar Kamboj was attended by Engineers-in-Chief of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh O.V. Ramesh Babu and K. Narasimha Murthy. The meeting prolonged from forenoon to evening but no decision was taken as there was no consensus on utilisation of water available in Nagarjunsagar reservoir.

In addition to the water indent placed by A.P. before the meeting for release of 9 tmc ft water from NS Right Canal, they also sought another 10 tmc ft water release from the reservoir for meeting the needs in the Krishna Delta System (KDS). On the other hand, Telangana asked for 21 tmc ft till February-end for drinking water needs of Hyderabad and other areas served by Nagarjunsagar.

Telangana ENC strongly opposed the indent for 10 tmc ft water requirement for KDS stating that they would not allow even a drop of water to the system as water requirements of KDS were not linked to Nagarjunsagar reservoir releases. Speaking after the meeting, Mr. Ramesh Babu said even the 9 tmc ft water sought from the Right Canal was also not justifiable as A.P. has enough water stored in Pulichintala reservoir.

He explained that Nagarjunsagar reservoir has only 45.4 tmc ft water above the minimum draw down level (MDDL) and of it 15 tmc ft is required for drinking needs of Hyderabad alone and the remaining 25 tmc ft was not sufficient to meet water unused so far by Telangana this water year. Further, he stated that Pulichintala has 26.75 tmc ft and Prakasam Barrage has another 2.44 tmc ft water available and water from Polavaram is also being drawn for the needs in the Krishna Basin through Pattiseema.

There was no justification in A.P.’s demand for 19 tmc ft water as it had received good spells of rain due to the three recent cyclones, the Telangana ENC said. He stated that they asked for a full board meeting at the earliest to discuss all issues.

As A.P. too stood ground with its demand suggesting that water could be drawn up to 490 ft level of Nagarjunsagar (534.4 ft level as at 6 pm on Monday), the three-member committee could not take any decision as Telangana insisted that water available in Nagarjunsagar below its MDDL was only for emergency needs.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 23 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 3-member panel meet of KRMB ends without taking any decision on water use

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Telangana strongly opposed to AP’s demand for release of Nagarjunsagar water for use in Krishna Delta System

The three-member committee of the Krishna River Management Board (KRMB) which met here on Monday to discuss the drinking water needs of the two member States — Andhra Pradesh and Telangana — for the next three months ended without taking any decision as Telangana strongly opposed A.P.’s indent of 19 tmc ft water, including 10 tmc ft for Krishna Delta System from Nagarjunasagar dam.

The meeting chaired by Member-Secretary of the river board Satish Kumar Kamboj was attended by Engineers-in-Chief of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh O.V. Ramesh Babu and K. Narasimha Murthy. The meeting prolonged from forenoon to evening but no decision was taken as there was no consensus on utilisation of water available in Nagarjunsagar reservoir.

In addition to the water indent placed by A.P. before the meeting for release of 9 tmc ft water from NS Right Canal, they also sought another 10 tmc ft water release from the reservoir for meeting the needs in the Krishna Delta System (KDS). On the other hand, Telangana asked for 21 tmc ft till February-end for drinking water needs of Hyderabad and other areas served by Nagarjunsagar.

Telangana ENC strongly opposed the indent for 10 tmc ft water requirement for KDS stating that they would not allow even a drop of water to the system as water requirements of KDS were not linked to Nagarjunsagar reservoir releases. Speaking after the meeting, Mr. Ramesh Babu said even the 9 tmc ft water sought from the Right Canal was also not justifiable as A.P. has enough water stored in Pulichintala reservoir.

He explained that Nagarjunsagar reservoir has only 45.4 tmc ft water above the minimum draw down level (MDDL) and of it 15 tmc ft is required for drinking needs of Hyderabad alone and the remaining 25 tmc ft was not sufficient to meet water unused so far by Telangana this water year. Further, he stated that Pulichintala has 26.75 tmc ft and Prakasam Barrage has another 2.44 tmc ft water available and water from Polavaram is also being drawn for the needs in the Krishna Basin through Pattiseema.

There was no justification in A.P.’s demand for 19 tmc ft water as it had received good spells of rain due to the three recent cyclones, the Telangana ENC said. He stated that they asked for a full board meeting at the earliest to discuss all issues.

As A.P. too stood ground with its demand suggesting that water could be drawn up to 490 ft level of Nagarjunsagar (534.4 ft level as at 6 pm on Monday), the three-member committee could not take any decision as Telangana insisted that water available in Nagarjunsagar below its MDDL was only for emergency needs.

3. articles.title: SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank retain D-SIB status; RBI maintains capital requirements
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The additional capital requirements are intended to enhance the resilience of these institutions.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has retained State Bank of India (SBI), HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank in its 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs), maintaining their respective positions under the same bucketing structure as in 2025.

Under the RBI’s framework, SBI, placed in Bucket 4, will have to maintain an additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital requirement of 0.80% of its Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs). HDFC Bank, classified under Bucket 2, will have an additional CET1 requirement of 0.40%, while ICICI Bank, placed in Bucket 1, will have to maintain 0.20%.
These additional capital requirements are over and above the Capital Conservation Buffer, strengthening the banks’ ability to absorb financial shocks and contain systemic risks.

The latest classification is based on data collected from banks as of March 31, 2026. Under the D-SIB framework, banks are categorised into different buckets according to their Systemic Importance Scores (SISs), with higher scores attracting higher additional capital requirements.

The RBI introduced the Framework for Dealing with D-SIBs on July 22, 2014, subsequently updating it on December 28, 2023. The framework requires the central bank to publicly disclose the names of designated D-SIBs annually, beginning in 2015, and assign them to appropriate buckets based on their systemic importance.

SBI and ICICI Bank were initially designated as D-SIBs in 2015 and 2016, respectively. HDFC Bank joined the list in 2017, when all three banks were identified as systemically important financial institutions.

articles.title: Zelenskyy calls for four-way talks with Russia ‘as soon as possible’
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: During a gathering of Ukrainian supporters in Berlin last week, U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said that Washington might consider offering Ukraine a security guarantee similar to that provided under Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty as part of a peace settlement.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday (November 23, 2026) called for new negotiations with Russia involving European leaders to be held as soon as possible and repeated a plea for his country to join the NATO alliance.
Mr. Zelenskyy, speaking by video to a gathering of lawmakers from NATO countries in Berlin, welcomed the latest push for peace talks with Moscow.
"We must do everything to make sure that the four-party meeting - Ukraine, Europe, America and Russia - happens as soon as possible. We are ready to do this. Literally tomorrow," Mr. Zelenskyy said.
"We have heard from our partners that they want to try to make it happen before Christmas. We hope it happens sooner."
European governments have been excluded from past discussions and their push to join talks has gained prominence in recent weeks.

Mr. Zelenskyy, whose country has been battling a full-scale Russian invasion since February 2022, has repeatedly called for a path to full membership in NATO - and not simply receiving security guarantees from alliance countries.
He argued that Ukraine's combat experience, innovative defence industry and large military would all benefit other allies.
"NATO is the answer - and with a strong Ukrainian army, NATO itself is guaranteed to be stronger," Mr. Zelenskyy told the Berlin gathering.
A number of NATO leaders have expressed hesitation about bringing Ukraine into the alliance.
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, speaking after Mr. Zelenskyy at the same event on Monday, underscored the alliance's support for Ukraine but noted that joining would require unanimous support.

articles.title: Nepal PM India visit LIVE: PM Modi announces offshore campus of IIT in Nepal
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Establishment of offshore IIT campus in Nepal, scholarships to Nepali students in India, a development package of over ₹15,000 crore for Nepal announced
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah flag off the ‘Saryu-Kamala Express’ via video conferencing, connecting Ayodhya with Janakpur.

Under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, the new direct rail link marks a significant step towards strengthening India-Nepal cultural and religious ties, boosting pilgrimage tourism and facilitating travel for devotees.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi gifted his Nepalese counterpart, Balendra Shah, a Kalamkari Sampoorna Ramayana painting, a Banarasi brocade stole in a Sadeli box, and ‘Gangajal’.
Mr. Modi gifted Mr. Shah the painting, depicting major episodes of Lord Rama’s journey, from his birth and exile to his victory over Ravana and return to Ayodhya, official sources said.

Hand-painted on cotton in the traditional Srikalahasthi style of Andhra Pradesh using a bamboo pen and natural dyes, the artwork showcases India’s rich heritage of storytelling, devotion and traditional craftsmanship.

It also symbolises the enduring spiritual and cultural bond between India and Nepal, connecting Ayodhya, the land of Lord Rama, with Janakpur, revered as the birthplace of Goddess Sita, and reflecting the shared heritage, friendship and values of the two nations.
Nepali PM Balendra Shah called on President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi.

Nepal PM Balen Shah, on an X post said, “With the aim of further strengthening our centuries-old historical relationship and making it relevant to the times, we have held in-depth, meaningful and far-reaching discussions on the many dimensions of our bilateral relations. During these discussions, important agreements on various areas of Nepal–India cooperation were reached, and infrastructure projects were inaugurated and had their foundation stones laid”.

“As a dependable and trusted neighbour, India consistently stood as the first responder in times of natural disasters and difficult times in Nepal,” Nepal PM Balen Shah said, adding that mutual respect, steadfast trust and unbroken goodwill are the bedrock of the relations.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while announcing the Development Cooperation Package of 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees, expressed his condolences over the loss of lives in the Nepal floods.

articles.title: Bangladesh garment makers eye 15% wage hike, far short of workers' demand
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Workers are demanding a rise in ‌the ⁠minimum monthly wage to 30,000 taka ($242) from 12,500 taka, citing soaring food, housing and ⁠transport costs

Bangladesh’s garment manufacturers could propose a roughly 15% ​increase in the minimum monthly wage at talks with authorities on Monday (September 23, 2026), industry ⁠leaders said, far short of workers’ demands for more than double their pay.

Since early November, unrest over wages has led to shutdowns and violence in the world’s second-largest garment exporter, which employs over 4 million ‌workers and provides supplies for major global retailers including H&M, Gap and Walmart. The protests over pay are testing the cost advantage of an industry that ‌generates more than 80% of the country’s export earnings.
Workers are demanding a rise in ‌the ⁠minimum monthly wage to 30,000 taka ($242) from 12,500 taka, citing soaring food, housing and ⁠transport costs.

Industry leaders, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the issue, said an increase of more than 15% would be unsustainable as the sector grapples with rising costs and weak ​global demand.
“Even then, many small factories ‌could struggle to cope with the increase,” one of the industry leaders said.
The industry has suffered significant losses from the unrest.

A survey by the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association found that disruptions over 18 days caused losses of about $428 million in 317 ‌factories, while international buyers shifted orders worth roughly $254 million to other countries amid concerns ​over production disruptions.
There was no immediate comment from the Labour Minister or workers’ representatives.

Higher production costs, rising utility tariffs and intense competition from rival apparel-producing countries ⁠limit manufacturers’ ability to absorb a substantially larger wage increase, industry leaders said.
Protests that began earlier this month forced hundreds of factories to close and led to clashes between workers and police, who ‌used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse demonstrators.

Bangladesh’s garment manufacturers could propose a roughly 15% ​increase in the minimum monthly wage at talks with authorities on Monday (September 23, 2026), industry ⁠leaders said, far short of workers’ demands for more than double their pay.

Since early November, unrest over wages has led to shutdowns and violence in the world’s second-largest garment exporter, which employs over 4 million ‌workers and provides supplies for major global retailers including H&M, Gap and Walmart. The protests over pay are testing the cost advantage of an industry that ‌generates more than 80% of the country’s export earnings.

Workers are demanding a rise in ‌the ⁠minimum monthly wage to 30,000 taka ($242) from 12,500 taka, citing soaring food, housing and ⁠transport costs.

Industry leaders, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the issue, said an increase of more than 15% would be unsustainable as the sector grapples with rising costs and weak ​global demand.

“Even then, many small factories ‌could struggle to cope with the increase,” one of the industry leaders said.

The industry has suffered significant losses from the unrest.

A survey by the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association found that disruptions over 18 days caused losses of about $428 million in 317 ‌factories, while international buyers shifted orders worth roughly $254 million to other countries amid concerns ​over production disruptions.

There was no immediate comment from the Labour Minister or workers’ representatives.

Higher production costs, rising utility tariffs and intense competition from rival apparel-producing countries ⁠limit manufacturers’ ability to absorb a substantially larger wage increase, industry leaders said.

Protests that began earlier this month forced hundreds of factories to close and led to clashes between workers and police, who ‌used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse demonstrators.

articles.title: U.S. panel urges India dialogue for Dalai Lama succession, warns of China legitimacy contest
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended establishing a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, arguing that China may turn the process into an international legitimacy contest

A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended setting up a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, contending that China may turn the process into an international contest over legitimacy.

A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended establishing a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, arguing that China may turn the process into an international legitimacy contest.

The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission, in a report to the U.S. Congress, made a strong pitch to recognise the Gaden Phodrang Trust as the sole legitimate authority to identify and recognise the successor to the 14th Dalai Lama.
The report by the bipartisan Commission said China was likely to use coercive tools to shape the outcome of the succession process.
It said that the U.S. Congress should adopt a policy of not recognising any successor to the Dalai Lama who is selected or installed by China.

“To carry out this policy and ensure U.S. government readiness for the Dalai Lama’s succession, Congress should direct the Secretary of State to… establish a senior-level channel with the Government of India for succession contingency planning, including intelligence sharing on Chinese influence operations,” the report said.

It also asked the U.S. Secretary of State to lead an internal interagency tabletop exercise on succession scenarios, with participation by the National Security Advisor, the Director of National Intelligence, and the Secretary of Defence.

The commission also asked the U.S. Secretary of State to conduct Track 1.5 and Track 2 dialogues and tabletop exercises with Indian counterparts on the political and security implications of succession scenarios.
The Commission also wanted the U.S. to coordinate with allies and partners on a diplomatic response that denies international legitimacy to any successor selected by China.

It also wanted the U.S. to counter succession-related influence operations by strengthening the Central Tibetan Administration’s cybersecurity and resilience against China’s cyber and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled disinformation campaigns.

articles.title: China says ready to work with India to facilitate visa issuance for business people
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The spokesperson’s remarks came amid reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals, including business visas

China has said it is ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both sides, amid reports that its diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance, including business visas, to Indian nationals.

"China issues visas for eligible foreign nationals coming to China in accordance with laws and regulations," a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson said in a written reply to questions by PTI about the reported reductions in visa issuance for Indians.
“We stand ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel of both sides," the spokesperson said.
The spokesperson's remarks came amid reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals, including business visas.

Also, fewer Indian businessmen were reportedly given visas to attend this month’s China Import Expo in Shanghai. The annual trade fair attracts businessmen from around the world to showcase their businesses to Chinese consumers.

Beijing has also stopped the service provider China Visa Application Centre from accepting visa applications, and its missions have begun handling them directly amid rising demand for Chinese visas, especially business visas.

The visa process between the two countries improved after India began issuing tourist visas to Chinese nationals in July last year after a gap of five years, amid efforts to repair bilateral ties that came under severe strain following the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in 2020.
The resumption of the visas was regarded as a significant move as the two countries started the normalisation process after a freeze in bilateral ties.
With liberalised visa processes, the two countries launched direct air services connecting several cities, including Beijing-New Delhi.
According to Indian officials, the visa rejection rate for Chinese nationals has been reduced to around 7% in recent months to encourage more business and tourism-related travel to India.

1. Core Context & Background: The spokesperson’s remarks came amid reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals, including business visas

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: China has said it is ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both sides, amid reports that its diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance, including business visas, to Indian nationals.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to Indian officials, the visa rejection rate for Chinese nationals has been reduced to around 7% in recent months to encourage more business and tourism-related travel to India.

A new study has found that DNA methylation, a natural process that acts like a "dimmer switch" to turn genes down or completely off, varies more than expected across different brain regions in genes linked to PTSD.

Three different regions of brain were analysed in each sample: the prefrontal cortex, involved in higher level functions, including decision-making, the amygdala or the emotional centre of the brain, and the hippocampus, which manages memory.

The study uncovered specific changes in the brain linked to PTSD, including a relative reduction in oligodendrocytes -- cells that form the protective covering of neurons (myelin sheath) -- in the amygdala of people with PTSD, particularly in those exposed to trauma in adulthood.
PTSD was also associated with more pronounced DNA methylation differences in the prefrontal cortex, while major depressive disorder was associated with methylation differences in the amygdala.

An incorrect or outdated spectacles prescription can leave a child’s vision inadequately corrected, affecting classroom activities and learning. fullParagraphs: Bausch + Lomb said it plans to discuss the results with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration as it considers next steps for the drug, including a potential late-stage trial

Bausch + Lomb said on Thursday its experimental eye-drop treatment failed to show a significant reduction in pain over the first 24 hours after laser eye surgery in a mid-stage study. articles.title: Antimicrobial overuse could make common infections harder to treat: Health ministry official
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: World AMR Awareness Week is observed from November 18 to 24 every year to improve awareness and understanding of antimicrobial resistance and promote best practices among the public, policymakers and One Health stakeholders

Misuse and overuse of antimicrobials could undermine decades of medical progress and make even common infections increasingly difficult to treat, a senior health ministry official said on Wednesday, calling for collective action to contain antimicrobial resistance (AMR).

Addressing the national observance of World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week 2026 virtually, Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava described AMR as one of the most serious public health challenges and stressed the need for a coordinated "One Health" approach to tackle it.
This year's theme is "One Health, One Action: Prevent AMR Now".
She said medicines that have saved countless lives are gradually losing their effectiveness due to misuse and overuse.

Srivastava highlighted the interconnectedness of human and animal health, plant and food systems and the environment, noting that improper use of antimicrobials across these sectors contributes to the emergence and spread of resistance.

She said the government has accorded high priority to containing AMR, with the National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance 2.0 (NAP AMR 2.0), 2025-2029, providing a framework for surveillance, infection prevention, responsible antimicrobial use, research and coordinated action.

The health ministry's National Programme on AMR Containment, coordinated by the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), focuses on strengthening laboratory capacity for AMR surveillance, infection prevention and control, antimicrobial stewardship and awareness generation, she said.

Srivastava urged healthcare professionals to prescribe antibiotics only when clinically indicated and in accordance with treatment guidelines. She also asked pharmacists to ensure appropriate dispensing against valid prescriptions and counsel patients on their correct use.

She also advised people against self-medication, sharing antibiotics or using leftover medicines, stressing that antibiotics are not effective against viral infections such as the common cold and influenza.
More than half of antimicrobial sales in India take place without prescriptions, while nearly half of outpatient antibiotic prescriptions are inappropriate, participants at the event noted.

articles.title: England launches world's largest AI-aided breast cancer screening trial
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Women attending routine breast screening at 30 planned sites nationwide will be given details about the trial and participate, unless they choose to opt out
England's state-run health service said Monday it has launched the world's largest AI-assisted breast cancer screening trial, which is set to involve nearly 700,000 women over the next three years.
The National Health Service (NHS) hailed the new trial as having the potential to transform breast cancer diagnosis, as it announced hundreds of women had been invited to take part at the outset.

The £10 million ($13 million) programme will assess if tools assisted by artificial intelligence can help improve early cancer detection in screening, which health officials hope will then free up specialist clinicians' time.
The AI-assisted reading tool will assist clinicians in reviewing images collected from routine mammograms, according to the NHS.

"This is the biggest AI breast cancer trial in the world," Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said in a statement, lauding the tech's "huge potential" while pledging "proper safeguards" to ensure safety and effectiveness.
"If successful, this technology could help women get a breast cancer diagnosis and start treatment much more quickly, giving them the best possible chance of recovery."
The trial is being led by the University of Warwick, the University of Cambridge and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, working closely with NHS England.
Women attending routine breast screening at 30 planned sites nationwide will be given details about the trial and participate, unless they choose to opt out.
The NHS stressed screening appointments will proceed as normal, but the AI-assisted tool will be used alongside specialists checking the images to look for cancers that are too small to see or feel.
The trial will test whether AI-assisted tools could allow most images to be reviewed by only one specialist, rather than the current two.

Women attending routine breast screening at 30 planned sites nationwide will be given details about the trial and participate, unless they choose to opt out

England's state-run health service said Monday it has launched the world's largest AI-assisted breast cancer screening trial, which is set to involve nearly 700,000 women over the next three years.

The National Health Service (NHS) hailed the new trial as having the potential to transform breast cancer diagnosis, as it announced hundreds of women had been invited to take part at the outset.

The £10 million ($13 million) programme will assess if tools assisted by artificial intelligence can help improve early cancer detection in screening, which health officials hope will then free up specialist clinicians' time.

The AI-assisted reading tool will assist clinicians in reviewing images collected from routine mammograms, according to the NHS.

"This is the biggest AI breast cancer trial in the world," Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said in a statement, lauding the tech's "huge potential" while pledging "proper safeguards" to ensure safety and effectiveness.

"If successful, this technology could help women get a breast cancer diagnosis and start treatment much more quickly, giving them the best possible chance of recovery."

The trial is being led by the University of Warwick, the University of Cambridge and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, working closely with NHS England.

Women attending routine breast screening at 30 planned sites nationwide will be given details about the trial and participate, unless they choose to opt out.

The NHS stressed screening appointments will proceed as normal, but the AI-assisted tool will be used alongside specialists checking the images to look for cancers that are too small to see or feel.

The trial will test whether AI-assisted tools could allow most images to be reviewed by only one specialist, rather than the current two.

articles.title: Oil and gas production to pick up in 4-5 years as recent measures take effect, Petroleum Ministry says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: In a note accessed by The Hindu, the Ministry has said that the oil and gas industry has a long gestation period and so exploration and finance decisions taken more than a decade ago are affecting the industry now

The government expects domestic oil and gas production to pick up in the next 4-5 years as several steps taken in the recent past begin to bear fruit in an industry typically characterised by long gestation periods, The Hindu has learnt.
According to an analysis by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, the current contraction in domestic oil and gas production is due to factors that took place more than a decade ago.

However, since then, the government has taken steps such as increasing drilling and exploration to record levels, changing laws and rules to provide stable terms to explorers, and opening new avenues for exploration.

“The steps taken in the last few years — new acreage, record drilling, deepwater wells and the revival of Mumbai High — will start showing up in production over the next three to four years,” the note asserted. “That is the nature of this sector: the decisions of one decade decide the output of the next.”
The note also argues that now, unlike earlier, the profits of oil and gas companies upstream companies like ONGC and Oil India are being used to fund exploration rather than subsidies.
“Until 2015, ONGC and Oil India were made to fund a large share of the subsidy on diesel, LPG and kerosene, through discounts on the crude they sold to oil marketing companies,” the note said.

According to data with the Ministry, ONGC paid ₹49,421 crore towards this subsidy in 2012-13 against a profit of ₹20,926 crore, and in 2013-14 paid ₹56,384 crore towards this subsidy against a net profit of ₹22,095 crore.

“In both years ONGC gave away more than twice what it earned,” the note said. “Money that should have gone into finding new oil and gas went into keeping retail prices down. This burden was ended from 2015-16. ONGC now keeps its earnings and has sharply raised its spending on exploration.”
According to the latest data on the Index of Core Industries, the oil and gas sectors have contracted continuously for 22 and 28 months, respectively.

“In this sector it takes five to ten years to go from awarding a block to first production,” a note prepared by the Ministry and accessed by The Hindu said. “Output in 2026 is the result of what was, and was not, done a decade ago.

articles.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after U.S. government input
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision”

Nvidia on Monday (November 23, 2026) reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after input from senior U.S. government officials left its board confident he posed no national security risk, less than two weeks after the co-founder resigned due to an alleged spy scandal.
U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision.”

The board voted unanimously to bring Mr. Huang back as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his “candor and ability to lead”, the company said in a statement.
Nvidia did not name the government officials it consulted or say what they told the board.

The decision came three days after Mr. Trump publicly urged Nvidia to take Mr. Huang back, calling him “one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world” and saying he would “love to see Jensen be given a second chance.”
Mr. Trump described Mr. Huang as “a good man” who “made some bad decisions" and said the company should rehire him “if they were smart".
Mr. Huang had offered to return, but the board initially refused.
Board chair Harvey Jones had said on an earnings call last week that directors had unanimously accepted his resignation and did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO".
“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Mr. Huang said, thanking the board, staff, shareholders and his family. “I can’t wait to get back to work.”

Mr. Huang, 63, stepped down on November 12 following reports that he had a relationship with Alice Huang — no relation — a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a company that bought billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia chips.

articles.title: Will use 'all available means' to counter U.S. blockade: Iran
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: War broke out between Iran and the United States on February 28 when U.S.-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei
Iran said on Monday (November 23, 2026) it would use all means at its disposal to counter a U.S. naval blockade that was imposed in retaliation for its own push to block the Strait of Hormuz.
"We will certainly not tolerate these actions and will use all available means to counter U.S. aggression," said Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei in a weekly press briefing.
War broke out between Iran and the United States on February 28 when U.S.-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
The conflict has since expanded after Iran retaliated with missile and drone strikes across the region, and with militant groups it backs in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq also entering the fray.
The Strait of Hormuz has become the focus of the conflict, with Iran continuing in its efforts to blockade the waterway, vital to global energy supplies.
In response, the U.S. imposed its own counterblockade of Iranian ports. It later announced a raft of economic sanctions, and launched a task force to disrupt land routes into Iran.

"You should bear in mind that what the Americans have described as economic sanctions, an economic blockade and a naval blockade undoubtedly constitutes an act of military aggression against Iran," said Mr. Baqaei.
"Under these circumstances, Iran is entitled, pursuant to Article 51 of the UN Charter, to use any means at its disposal to defend itself."
Iranian forces have made multiple announcements in recent weeks of ships catching fire attempting to use routes that Tehran considers off-limits.
Diplomatic efforts to resolve the crisis remain stalled, especially since the collapse of a June deal that laid out a pathway to a permanent settlement.

articles.title: Severe anaemia affects less than 2% of population: ICMR survey
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: SAMPADA covered more than 2 lakh individuals from over 81,000 households across 183 districts in 35 States and Union Territories

According to a survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), severe anaemia was observed in less than 2% of people in the majority of age groups. The Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA) 2023-2025 was released on Monday (November 23, 2026).

It showed that children aged 12-59 months had 42% anaemia prevalence, adolescent girls aged 10-19 years had anaemia prevalence of 46%, adolescent boys aged 10-19 years and men aged 20–59 years had 22-23% anaemia prevalence, whereas women of reproductive age had 56% prevalence.
The survey also found that mild anaemia constitutes a substantial proportion of the overall anaemia burden.

“SAMPADA provides nationally representative estimates of anaemia across children, adolescents, adults, pregnant and lactating women and older adults, together with detailed information on micronutrient deficiencies to evaluate potential causes of anaemia. It is encouraging that prevalence of anaemia is lower in SAMPADA compared to previous national surveys. The comprehensive anaemia profiling in the SAMPADA survey provides an evidence base to strengthen the ongoing national efforts towards Anaemia Mukt Bharat,” said Rajiv Bahl, secretary, Department of Health Research.

The report noted that about half of anaemic women, including pregnant and lactating women, adolescent girls, and children, have mild anaemia, indicating considerably lower risk of serious health consequences than moderate or severe anaemia. Anaemia prevalence is much lower among adolescent boys, adult and older men, and even among those affected, three-fourths have only mild anaemia, said the release issued by the Union Health Ministry.

SAMPADA represents one of the largest and most comprehensive nutrition surveys undertaken globally. The survey covered more than 2 lakh individuals from over 81,000 households across 183 districts in 35 States and Union Territories. More than 1.7 lakh blood samples were analysed for haemoglobin estimation across different age, sex, and physiological groups.

“A major strength of SAMPADA is the use of gold standard method of venous blood sampling and automated analysers for haemoglobin estimation, providing greater accuracy and reproducibility. In a sub-sample, the survey also assessed iron status, folate, vitamin B12, together with inflammatory biomarkers C-reactive protein (CRP) and alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AGP) to obtain national level prevalence estimates,” the release said.
Iron deficiency accounts for about half of the anaemia cases in women, adolescent girls, and children, said the report.

The micronutrient assessment showed that although iron deficiency is the predominant contributor to anaemia in vulnerable population groups, it accounts for about half of the overall anaemia burden, highlighting the need to simultaneously address multiple nutritional and non-nutritional causes of anaemia, including infections, hemoglobinopathies, and inflammation related to chronic disease.

However, the prevalence of vitamin B12 and folate deficiency was similar in both anaemic and non-anaemic individuals across population groups, indicating a limited contribution of these micronutrient deficiencies to anaemia in India.

articles.title: Testing times: On India’s two-Test series against New Zealand
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India needs to be at its best in Tests against New Zealand

New Zealand at home remains an indomitable cricketing opposition. Even the great West Indian squad led by Clive Lloyd suffered a 0-1 Test series defeat in 1980. Pitches that look lush as English meadows, the wind that is often bone-chilling cold, and fast bowlers relishing their prospects, make any tour of New Zealand a difficult outing. So far, the visiting Indians have done well, having won the T20I and ODI series, but the real contest starts with the first Test at Wellington’s Basin Reserve from Thursday. The Shubman Gill-led men’s last overseas tour of Sri Lanka ended with a middling 1-0 victory in the two Tests, but more needs to be done against New Zealand in the latest two-Test series. Placed fourth in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) table, and with hopes of securing a final berth seemingly fragile, India is in a win-all-games situation first up against New Zealand and later when Australia arrives next year. Against current WTC topper New Zealand, the Indian batters have to stay anchored. This is a line-up that no longer has Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Cheteshwar Pujara and Ajinkya Rahane. Gill and company get another opportunity to reiterate their credentials.

For some rugged inspiration they need not look beyond coach Gautam Gambhir in their dressing room. The doughty former India opener batted for 643 minutes while scoring a match-saving 137 in the Napier Test during the 2009 tour. The southpaw will be hoping that the current batting unit, which is high on flair, will remain sober and effectively counter the host. K.L. Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal and Gill have the onerous task of negating the New Zealand seamers in their backyard. Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel add depth, and if the former can successfully unleash his maverick batting approach, India can upset the host’s best-laid plans. New Zealand will miss the retired Kane Williamson but its batters would be comfortable on familiar surfaces. For India, much would hinge on how Jasprit Bumrah bowls. If the spearhead clicks, then it becomes easier for much of his support-cast that includes the persevering Mohammed Siraj, who was a touch rusty in Sri Lanka. From the squads of the past to the present unit, Ravindra Jadeja remains the link. Whether he will get a role to play or whether the management prefers an all-pace attack, remains a matter of conjecture. The home team led by Tom Latham will depend on Matt Henry, Kyle Jameson and other pacers, to choke the Indian batters. A hard task awaits India, first at Wellington and then at Christchurch.

articles.title: Many imperatives: On India’s Asia diplomacy
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India must shore up its partnerships in the Asian region

Each year, the summits of the 11-member Association of South-East Asian Nations mark an important moment on the diplomatic calendar: India is able to interact with all of its partners in the Indo-Pacific and engage global powers at the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s talks with Indo-Pacific players focused on a future shaped “not by competition, but by cooperation”. This year, the summit in Manila hosted by the Philippines had many other imperatives. These were the first ASEAN summits since the U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran and Iran’s Hormuz blockade and strikes on Gulf countries that have upended energy and trade across South and South East Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world during the EAS was aimed as much at leaders from the U.S., Russia and China as it was for the region. articles.title: Amid cold wave, students’ indefinite strike against J&K recruitment board scam gathers steam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘Students and Aga sahib were removed from the site against their will; the demand stands: a fair probe into the alleged FAA rigging; this fight isn’t over,’ said a protester

Protesting government job aspirants on Saturday (November 21, 2026) launched an indefinite strike in Srinagar amid a cold wave over the government’s failure to act against the J&K Service Selection Board (JKSSB), the main recruitment agency of J&K that has become mired in a cheating scam that has led to 16 arrests so far.

While former Member of Parliament (MP) Aga Syed Ruhullah joined the protesters in Srinagar, other regional parties also demanded the cancellation of all examinations held by the Board and called for “fixing the responsibility”.

The peaceful sit-in was forcibly broken up by police on Saturday night (November 21), said the protesters. “Students and Aga sahib were removed from the site against their will. The demand stands: a fair probe into the alleged FAA [Finance Accounts Assistant] rigging. This fight isn’t over,” said one protester.
Speaking at the Sher-i-Kashmir Park earlier, Mr. Ruhullah said the protest is a “rare effort to open up space where youth could fight for their rights”.

“We demand that heads must roll. We have the elected government and an unelected government ruling J&K. Both share responsibility for it. Unfortunately, there is a sense of complacency. The examinations should be postponed, responsibility for the irregularities fixed and reforms carried out. The administration should engage students and address their concerns,” said Mr. Ruhullah.

Mr. Ruhullah joined scores of students and aspirants who held a sit-in all day in Srinagar. With evening temperature dipping, a spokesman of Mr. Ruhullah said, “There was no food or blankets. No entry. Students on a peaceful sit-in are being frozen out on a bitter Srinagar night. Their only crime is asking for justice over the alleged Finance Accounts Assistant recruitment rigging.”
The night temperature has dipped to around zero degrees Celsius in Srinagar amid a severe cold wave.
On November 15, the J&K Police busted four “cheating modules” in Jammu during the Board’s examination for the FAA posts.

Nearly 1.62 lakh aspirants had appeared for around 600 posts across J&K. Besides 16 arrests made in the case, the police said it filed three First Information Reports (FIRs) and recovered eight wireless devices, 22 mobile phones and four vehicles of the accused.

However, Board chairman Shrikant Balasaheb Suse said the “examination was not compromised by a paper leak or mass malpractice” and announced that the upcoming exams will be held “as per the schedule”.

articles.title: Vasan urges political parties to fight for Cauvery water rights
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tamil Maanila Congress (Moopanar) president G.K. Vasan on Saturday urged the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) to direct the Karnataka government to release water due to Tamil Nadu. He also sought the cooperation of political parties in Tamil Nadu in securing the State’s rights by setting aside their differences.
In a statement, Mr. Vasan expressed shock over the Supreme Court dismissing Tamil Nadu’s plea seeking the release of 11 thousand million cubic feet of Cauvery water by Karnataka.
He said that, in the past, the Karnataka government had not complied with the directions of the CWMA and had acted in a step-motherly manner.

Farmers in the Cauvery delta are under severe economic distress due to an acute shortage of water for irrigation. The Karnataka government should understand that the Cauvery water-sharing issue and the Mekedatu issue are not only river water disputes, but also the lifelines of the people of Tamil Nadu, Mr. Vasan added.

He also sought the cooperation of political parties in Tamil Nadu in securing the State’s rights by setting aside their differences.

articles.title: Municipal staff transfers to move online by Tamil Nadu govt., with vacancies displayed on portal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to the guidelines, general transfers will ordinarily be conducted between April 1 and May 31 every year. Applications will be received through the online portal between March 1 and 31. Employees who have completed three years of service in a post or station will be eligible for transfer during this period, subject to the availability of vacancies.

The Tamil Nadu government has introduced online counselling for transfers and postings of employees in municipal corporations, municipal councils and town panchayats, covering employees in the lower and middle levels of the government pay structure, including posts such as assistants, junior assistants and superintendents. The guidelines were issued through two Government Orders (G.O.s) by the Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department dated November 19, 2026.
The counselling will be based on vacancies and station seniority. The online portal is being developed by the respective heads of departments and will be introduced shortly, an official said.

Regarding whether employees would be able to raise grievances relating to seniority or other issues through the portal, the official said the department would be asked to incorporate a provision for submitting representations online. The portal would also provide details of vacancies and the procedure for applying for transfers, he said.

According to the guidelines, general transfers will ordinarily be conducted between April 1 and May 31 every year. Applications will be received through the online portal between March 1 and 31. Employees who have completed three years of service in a post or station will be liable for transfer during this period, subject to the availability of vacancies.

Transfers during the non-transfer period, between June 1 and March 31, will be permitted only on administrative grounds, including promotions, disciplinary reasons, complaints, long leave arrangements and other administrative exigencies.

All transfers, including those sought by employees, during the transfer period will be processed through the online portal. The guidelines also provide for a maximum of three alternative station preferences in transfer applications.
The official said counselling for Executive Officers of town panchayats had already been conducted and postings issued based on it.

articles.title: AIPC Tamil Nadu to support MSMEs through professional network
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The All India Professionals’ Congress (AIPC) Tamil Nadu chapter should function as a professional support network for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), helping them access legal, financial and technical expertise, said its national chairman Madhu Goud Yaskhi at the organisation’s annual summit in Chennai on Saturday.

Mr. Yaskhi proposed that chartered accountants, lawyers, engineers and IT professionals associated with the AIPC volunteer their time to help MSMEs with taxation, regulatory compliance, financial management and delayed payments.

He said over ₹7 lakh crore owed to small enterprises across India remained stuck in delayed payments, with large companies often taking more than 120 days to clear dues despite the statutory 45-day limit.

The AIPC could also take up delayed payments by State public sector undertakings with the Tamil Nadu government, he said. Lawyers could help MSMEs pursue their dues through legal notices, while chartered accountants could assist with invoice discounting and compliance.
Outgoing AIPC chairman and Rajya Sabha MP Praveen Chakravarty said Congress needed to reconnect with professionals in major urban centres, where it had lost electoral ground since 2014, he said.

He also urged professionals to help implement and promote the Tamil Nadu government’s policies, including the Private University Bill, startup initiatives and tourism projects, saying the Congress’s participation in the coalition government brought responsibilities beyond its share in the Cabinet.
After the event, Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan told reporters that the Private University Bill passed by the Assembly had received the Governor’s assent.

The government would prepare a standard operating procedure and issue guidelines for its implementation, he said. The legislation aimed to attract foreign universities to Tamil Nadu and provide students access to international-standard educational facilities within the State.
Lok Sabha MP C. Robert Bruce and Rajya Sabha MP Christopher Tilak were present.

articles.title: Gandhi is the core ideological enemy of the Sangh Parivar: Ramachandra Guha
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: While early years after Independence in India saw excessive veneration of Gandhi, the recent trends have shifted to a “venomous detestation” of the man by the right-wing ecosystem led by the Sangh Parivar, historian Ramachandra Guha said here on Saturday while discussing his latest book Arguments with Gandhi.

“When I was young, the ethos in India was excessive veneration of Gandhi. Now, it has become parricide,” he told the audience. “For the Sangh Parivar – it includes the BJP, the RSS, all BJP cabinet ministers – the demon is Gandhi. That should be very evident from whatever they say about Gandhi. Actually, Gandhi is their core ideological enemy, as he has once been of the Left.” Dr. Guha averred. Citing an analogy, he said that Prime Minister Modi, in his article on Gandhi in the New York Times on his 150th birth anniversary, “praised him for everything except Hindu-Muslim harmony”. Mr. Modi, he said, seem to think that he needs to praise Gandhi because he is a global figure, but the hardcore footsoldiers of the Sangh Parivar detest Gandhi venomously. He was in conversation with Tamil author and novelist B. Jeyamohan.

Elaborating on the reasons for such attacks on Gandhi, Dr. Guha emphasised that Gandhi had come to represent the feminine in the eyes of the “macho Right”, what with his non-violent policy, inter-faith harmony, his scepticism of the State, or his scepticism of progress.

“Gandhi raises almost all the important questions of human existence today. You can think of no other thinker; he catches so many vital aspects of our lives,” Dr. Guha observed, as the conversation veered towards his ideas of non-violent science which influenced several scientists, including J.B.S. Haldane and Laurie Baker. Gandhi, he said, derived his principles from all traditions and belief systems – Jainism, Vaishnavism, Christianity, and even communism. His attitude to gender, religion, or non-violence evolved through his engagements with various philosophies.

“I do not see him as a quintessentially Hindu thinker, quintessentially Indian thinker, [or] quintessentially traditional thinker. He transcends these lanes. Or Leftist, Rightist, Conservative; he is all three,” Dr. Guha added.

On the question of caste and the equations with the Ambedkarite principles, Dr. Guha said that Gandhi was a guilt-ridden upper caste while Ambedkar was a dalit without emancipation and they could only take those paths. From the perspective of history and the future of India, the paths are converging. Asked if Gandhi’s methods are lost in the era of social media, he said the “cockroaches showed that they have it”. If the book came out a few months later, he said he would have added a few paragraphs on the Cockroach Janata Party movement.

articles.title: T.N. may see solar energy installations slowing down, say energy generators
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In the last one month, some of the solar energy generators received notices demanding 8% banking charges.
Tamil Nadu, which has 10,000 MW-11,000 MW of installed solar energy capacity, may see a slowdown in solar energy installations in 2027, according to industry representatives.

The single window system for obtaining approvals is not functioning effectively, finer details based on the recently-announced Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Policy should be notified by the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission, and costs are escalating, say solar energy investors.

“No approvals have been granted for solar energy projects for almost six months now. Only now has the government started accepting the applications. Even if they are approved now, it is difficult to commission the projects by March 2027. From April next year, it is mandatory for all new projects to have BESS, and this will push the costs up,” said one of the solar energy investors in Coimbatore.

“We had a detailed discussion with the TNERC on the BESS policy. The policy says there will be waiver of wheeling charges. The wheeling charges are applicable only if a consumer buys under open access. However, the policy says solar energy generators who store energy can sell it only to the State utility. There are many such issues with the policy that need better clarity in the policy ,” says AD Thirumoorthy, State Level Renewable Energy Committee Member, Government of Tamil Nadu.

The single window approval system is functioning effectively for solar energy projects that come as a part of foreign direct investments. The others require multiple approvals, starting right from the rural local body heads. These lead to delays, pushing up the costs, he added.

While the BESS policy is a welcome move, the Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation should ensure that stored solar energy is evacuated within 24 hours, so that the generator can store freshly generated energy the next day, said L. Santhosh, president of the Tamil Nadu Electricity Consumers Association.

In the last one month, some of the solar energy generators received notices demanding 8% banking charges. These are not applicable because the court has stayed the green energy open access policy of the State, he added. More sub-stations and solutions for right of way challenges to lay lines on lands belonging to various government departments are among the other issues faced by investors that threaten to slow down solar energy projects.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh gets national recognition for its progress in HIV/AIDS control
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Six districts in the State have achieved ‘Surakshit’ status and another 10 the ‘Saksham’ status, and the rankings are based on a district’s performance on 95-95-95 targets fixed by the Joint United Nations Programme
Andhra Pradesh has received national recognition for its progress in controlling HIV, with six districts in the State achieving the ‘Surakshit’ status and another 10 achieving the ‘Saksham’ status.

According to a release from the department, the districts of Chittoor, East Godavari, Guntur, Kakinada, Visakhapatnam and Vizianagaram achieved ‘Surakshit’ status, while the districts of Anakapalli, Anantapur, Bapatla, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, Eluru, Kurnool, Parvathipuram-Manyam, Srikakulam, Tirupati and YSR Kadapa achieved the ‘Saksham’ status.
The rankings are based on a district’s performance on 95-95-95 targets, fixed by the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS(UNAIDS) as part of efforts to end the epidemic by 2030.

The three targets include ensuring that 95% of people living with HIV know their status, providing antiretroviral therapy (ART) to 95% of those diagnosed; and achieving viral suppression in 95% of those receiving treatment.

According to the release, the percentage of people living with HIV who knew their status increased from 87.7% in April 2026 to 92.7% in October, and currently stands at 92.8%. Between April and October, 7,641 new HIV cases were identified through Integrated Counselling and Testing Centres.
The number of people receiving ART increased from 2,41,507 in April to 2,65,690 in October, an additional 24,183 patients. Viral suppression has been achieved in 96.4% of those undergoing treatment.
Reacting to the development, Minister for Health, Medical and Family Welfare Satya Kumar Yadav said 16 districts improved their performance between April and October.

The release stated that the A.P. State AIDS Control Society (APSACS) developed ‘Suraksha’ portal to monitor HIV testing, diagnosis and treatment services. It also launched ‘Each One Reach One’ initiative, to bring patients who had discontinued medication back into treatment. These two measures also helped the State achieve the targets.
Mr. Satya Kumar said priority was to ensure timely diagnosis, continuous treatment and quality healthcare without discrimination for everyone living with HIV.
APSACS Project Director Smaran Raj said the organisation was committed to bringing three more districts to ‘Surakshit’ status in the week.

articles.title: 14-year-old used AI chatbot to hack Agniveer ‘test’ website, wanted to earn money by selling it on dark web: Delhi police sources
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Haryana teenager used an AI chatbot to identify valuable data and find a way into the test portal; preliminary investigation suggests only names and addresses were accessed, Delhi Police sources say

A 14-year-old boy from Haryana’s Ballabhgarh, who was apprehended for attempting to sell sensitive information linked to around 4,000 Agniveer personnel on the dark web, used artificial intelligence tools to “identify data that could fetch him money and sought the chatbot’s help to hack into a website”, a senior official familiar with the investigation told The Hindu .
The boy gained unauthorised access to a test website designed for former Agniveers to register themselves and explore employment opportunities in the Indian Armed Forces.

“Preliminary investigation has revealed that the boy managed to breach only the test website, gaining access to names and addresses. There is no indication so far that information relating to marks, ranks, results or other sensitive personnel records was compromised,” the official said.
During preliminary questioning, the boy told investigators that he was motivated by the prospect of making money.

“He said he first asked an AI chatbot to identify what kind of data could help him earn money. He then sought its assistance in finding a way to hack into the system and access such information,” the official said. The exact method used to gain access to the website is still being examined.

After accessing the website, the boy allegedly extracted the information and advertised it on a dark web marketplace, claiming to possess personal records of around 4,000 Agniveer personnel and sought $500 for the purported database.

The Delhi Police’s Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) unit has recovered data from the juvenile’s digital devices. Investigators are now examining the material to establish its authenticity and determine the extent of the suspected breach.

The IFSO unit has also written to the National Informatics Centre (NIC), seeking clarification on the data available on the test website and the information accessed by the boy. The police are awaiting a response to ascertain precisely what information may have been compromised.

While the NIC provides digital infrastructure and hosts government portals, the ownership and maintenance of Agniveer personnel records rest with the Armed Forces and the concerned ministries, officials said.
As the accused is a juvenile, he was counselled and handed over to his parents. The police are consulting the Juvenile Justice Board on the further course of action.

articles.title: Three cyclones in three weeks: What’s happening in the Bay of Bengal? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Such a frequency is uncommon but not unique this year; there were around 1.8 cyclones a year in the post-monsoon period in 1982-2022, with the average increasing after 2001

The story so far: Within 23 days this year, three cyclones formed over the Bay of Bengal. Of them, Cyclone Arnab made landfall near Yanam on the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28 and Murasu on November 3 near Ongole. Cyclone Akvan formed on November 16 and made landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha on Friday morning (November 20, 2026).

A cyclone requires an atmospheric disturbance, abundant moisture, and favourable winds. The Bay has two main cyclone seasons, April-May and October-December. During the southwest monsoon, strong winds blowing in different directions at different altitudes suppress cyclone formation. But as the monsoon withdraws, the vertical wind shear weakens even as the waters remain warm, creating more favourable conditions.
